text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.3% today, bouncing back from a three-day dip that had taken the stock down about 1%. The rebound aligns with two major developments: crude prices jumped notably, with global oil hitting $113.96 per barrel (versus the U.S. benchmark at $96.16), and Trump publicly pressured South Korea to invest in the Alaska LNG project, signaling U.S. political will to move forward on major energy infrastructure deals that would benefit large producers like ConocoPhillips.

The timing also reflects tightening supply conditions despite recent efforts to ease them. While the G7 announced diesel reserves releases earlier in the week, Saudi Aramco's warning that rebuilding global oil stockpiles could take up to two years—worsened by the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict disrupting Middle East shipping—suggests sustained upward pressure on prices ahead, which supports the stock's recovery over the past week.
